idea: q-major derivative table, float2/float4 term loads in wprime
numbers: lab wprime 0.913 (5060 Ti), A100 0.898 at degree 10; step on top of degree 5: Ada 1.027, 5060 Ti 1.070, A100 1.040
reason: fewer load instructions; the gain disappears with fewer terms.
notes: Fuller record says REJECTED on Ada with the A100 still open and gives Ada step 0.9909 (float2) and 1.0276 (float4); the index shows Ada 1.027 only.

idea: wprime reads the stored w with `__ldcs`
numbers: lab wprime 0.964 (5060 Ti), 1.127 (Ada), 0.982 (Ada, degree 5); step 0.987 (5060 Ti), 1.005 (A100-SXM4, degree 5)
reason: helps where L2 is small relative to the slabs (sm_120), hurts on sm_89.
notes: Contradiction: fuller record says Status PENDING with only lab numbers (0.964-0.966, 1.127); index says REJECTED and gives step numbers not found in the fuller record.

idea: The fused forward stores w with `__stcs`

notes: Fuller record says Status PENDING and Step pending; only the index row has step numbers. Its Why (keeps W, a and x in L2) is a rationale, not a stated rejection reason.

idea: `edge_outer_sum` chunk sizes 64
numbers: Ada step 1.002 (forward chunk 64), 1.004 (backward block 64)
notes: Contradiction: fuller record says Status PENDING, Measured pending, Why empty and Date 3 November 2026; the index row gives Ada step numbers and date 2026-11-04.

idea: Two-warp 32x64 / 64x32 tiles for the CUTLASS 3×TF32 GEMMs (A100)
reason: wave quantisation on 108 SMs; the smaller tiles mainloops lose more than the even load gains.
notes: Fuller record gives MD step b/a 1.0144 / 1.0116 (32x64) and 1.0167 / 1.0173 (64x32), consistent with the index.

idea: W slice split into TF32 parts once per block (tensor-core forward, A100)
numbers: fused forward A100-SXM4 1.362 (12 -> 8 warps), RTX 5060 Ti 1.707 (2 -> 4 parts); bitwise; bound F-tc-no-wsplit 0.862
reason: the doubled slice costs a third of the block's warps; the latency hiding lost outweighs the split instructions saved.
notes: Fuller record gives the kernel-lab ratios in one process (base 3.688 ms, pre-split 5.023 ms); the switch is a lab variant with no MD A/B recorded.

idea: The species GEMM in our own mma.sync 3xTF32 kernel (for the A100)
numbers: kernel lab vs Triton: A100 0.94 (16p), Ada 0.91, 5060 Ti 0.86; step A100-SXM4 1.003 / 1.002 vs default (Triton species GEMM 0.992), Ada 1.001 / 0.999 vs Triton species GEMM
reason: a simple mma.sync kernel only reaches Triton's rate; CUTLASS 3xTF32 is about 2.7x faster per product, and closing the gap needs a CUTLASS-class grouped GEMM for at most about 5 % of the A100 step.
notes: Fuller record gives lab times in microseconds (A100 Triton 591.5, tc16 594.7) and the step pair against the default; the 5060 Ti has a lab figure only.

idea: The species GEMM as one gathered CUTLASS 3xTF32 launch (A100)
numbers: step A100-SXM4 0.9928 / 0.9922 vs default (Triton species GEMM 0.992); lab size 16 CUTLASS 678 us vs Triton 597, bound 207
reason: in the captured MD step the A100's concatenated CUTLASS product is cheap; the grouped versions lose the rest to per-call row ordering and indices.
notes: Fuller record also gives RTX 4000 Ada lab size 16 932 vs Triton 936 us, which the index row omits; the status is kept as an A/B switch.

idea: wprime backward over edges sorted by (pair, r), so edges of one derivative-table slab run together
numbers: lab wprime 1.513 (RTX 5060 Ti; slope alone 0.757)
reason: the kernel streams edges in receiver order; sorted by slab, the output gradients and sender atomics lose locality, which costs more than the whole slope.
notes: Switch is none; the bound permutes inputs for the unchanged kernel, sort cost not counted. Fuller record gives base 8.30 ms, piece-sorted 12.55 ms, no slope 6.28 ms.

idea: wprime slope as dr = a'(r) . (dw W) instead of the per-edge G' slab
numbers: A100-SXM4: the da = dw W product alone 2.27 ms (CUTLASS 3xTF32), 4.14 ms (FP32) against the slope's 1.81 ms
reason: the reformulation moves 61 GFLOP of per-edge products into the backward; at the A100's 3xTF32 rate that alone costs more than the table reads it saves.
notes: Not built; the bound timed one large GEMM of Benchmark_loup shape. Fuller record also gives cuBLAS TF32 1.27 ms, rejected as too inexact (about 1e-3).

idea: First interaction's radial table stores only the columns it uses
numbers: step A100-SXM4 1.002 / 0.999, RTX 5060 Ti 1.002; bitwise
baseline: computing the full width and slicing
notes: The fuller record has no Why bullet, so no rejection reason is stated. Fuller Measured gives A100 1.0018 / 0.9993 (Modal) and RTX 5060 Ti 1.002.

idea: 3×FP16 m16n8k16 MMAs in the tensor-core forward; 8 or 10 warps
numbers: lab A100 1.197 (bound of its big·big product 0.964), 5060 Ti 1.07; 8 / 10 warps 1.160 / 1.109
reason: the MMAs are not the limit, and fewer warps lose more latency hiding than the spills cost.
notes: Lab only; the kernel lab variants are tc-fp16, tc-warps8 and tc-warps10. The fuller record notes 104 B spills on the A100.

idea: cp.async double-buffered a / sh (and x) staging in the fused forward
numbers: lab A100-SXM4 tc-prefetch 1.071 / 1.038, tc-prefetch-x 1.152; 5060 Ti 0.861 (tc), 0.930 (SIMT); Ada SIMT 1.025
reason: the A100 kernel is at 168 registers with 12 warps; the second buffer costs warps or spills, and the 12 warps already hide the load latency.
notes: Fuller record gives re-screen timings: A100 tc-prefetch 1.255, tc-prefetch-x 1.384; 5060 Ti simt-prefetch 1.013 (bitwise). Kept off everywhere; index row shows the earlier lab numbers.

idea: Radial table launch shapes (BLOCK_E, COLUMN_BLOCK, warps)
numbers: best 0.925 of 271 µs on the A100 PCIe (about 20 µs)
reason: too small to pass an MD A/B.

idea: Fewer coefficient multiplies in the fused forward's tensor product
notes: Status says bound, but the 0.961 is a lab falsifier that drops all coefficient multiplies, so the stage is taken as lab. The fuller record has no Why bullet.

idea: Interaction 2's radial table evaluated inside the fused forward
numbers: about 4.5 GB of L2 traffic per force call against 0.77 GB now
reason: the table is cheap to store once and expensive to re-evaluate per warp.
notes: Estimate only; not built. The fuller record also cites an A100 falsifier: stored-a loads bounded at 0.900 of the forward, VEC_A reaches 0.903.

idea: 3xFP16 GEMMs (one FP16 GEMM over 3K, power-of-two scaling) instead of CUTLASS 3xTF32
numbers: A100-SXM4-80GB GEMM 0.49–0.66 of the CUTLASS 3xTF32 time; error relative to |A| |B| 1.1–2.0e-6 against 3xTF32 1.1–2.7e-7 and FP32 0.8–4.2e-7
reason: the FP16 MMA accumulates more coarsely; the split would have to be fused into every producer for any gain.
notes: Error measured against float64 in the GEMM bench, not a force check. Fuller record also cites results/round4-staging-20261105/ and gives the unfused split at 78-138 us per call.

idea: The fused forward's tensor product as a second 3xTF32 mma (w x from the product's fragments, S = CG sh, edges as k)
numbers: lab A100-SXM4 1.276 (bound without TP 0.617), 5060 Ti 1.64; message 4-6e-7 rms of FP32
reason: each A element feeds one mma triple (N = 8 outputs, K = 8 edges), and its preparation costs about what the FP32 TP terms cost.
notes: Rejected and kept off in the code. The 5060 Ti figure is with tensor cores forced on, per the record.

idea: Cache hints in the fused forward (x evict_last / ldg, a and sh no_allocate)
notes: Fuller record gives lab forward x-ldg 1.021, x-el 1.021, tc-a4 with hints 0.912-0.923, RTX 5060 Ti 0.996. It has no Why bullet, so no rejection reason is stated.

idea: Morton atom order for the x gathers
numbers: 5060 Ti forward 6,724 (repeat), 6,737 (Morton), 6,679 µs (shuffled)
reason: x (10 MB) stays in L2 in any order; the gathers cost latency, not DRAM traffic.
notes: Fuller record adds that the x gathers cost 0.837 of the A100 forward (falsifier). Structure files are under results/round4-staging-20261105/orders/.
